entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Suez Crisis, a pivotal event in modern history, occurred in 1956 when Israel, the United Kingdom, and France invaded Egypt, sparking a global conflict. 

The invasion, led by Israeli Prime Minister David Ben-Gurion and British Prime Minister Anthony Eden, aimed to regain control of the Suez Canal, a strategic waterway connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea through Egypt. 

The crisis escalated into a full-blown war, involving the United States, the Soviet Union, and other international actors. 

The Suez Crisis led to the withdrawal of the invading forces, the nationalization of the Suez Canal, and a shift in the global balance of power, marking a significant turning point in the Cold War.
